commands.stdout:
# Composio Dev

Load this file only when the user explicitly needs developer-project workflows. Do not lead with `composio dev` for ordinary top-level CLI usage.

## Use `dev init` To Bind A Directory

Use `composio dev init` when the user wants to attach the current directory to a developer project.

If later commands complain about missing developer project context, come back to `dev init`.

```bash
composio dev init -y --no-browser
```

## Inspect Toolkits And Versions

Use toolkit commands to inspect developer-scoped capabilities:

```bash
composio dev toolkits list
composio dev toolkits info github
composio dev toolkits search "email"
composio dev toolkits version github
```

## Manage Auth Configs

Use auth-config commands when the user is configuring developer-project authentication behavior:

```bash
composio dev auth-configs list
```

## Manage Connected Accounts

Use developer connected-account commands when the user is working with developer-project users or auth-config-specific flows.

Top-level `composio link` is consumer-only. Use `dev connected-accounts link` for developer-project flows.

```bash
composio dev connected-accounts list
```

## Work With Triggers

Use trigger commands when the user is creating, inspecting, or listening to developer-project triggers.

```bash
composio dev triggers list
composio dev triggers info AGENT_MAIL_NEW_EMAIL_TRIGGER
```

## Inspect Logs

Use logs when the user is debugging tool executions or trigger deliveries inside a developer project.

```bash
composio dev logs tools
composio dev logs triggers
```

## Switch Or Inspect Org And Project Context

Use these commands when the user needs to confirm or change the active developer scope:

If the user only wants to connect and execute tools as an end user, return to the top-level workflow instead of staying in `composio dev`.

```bash
composio dev orgs list
composio dev projects list
```

DESCRIPTION
  Developer workflows: init, playground execution, logs, projects, toolkits, accounts, and triggers.

USAGE
  composio dev <subcommand> [flags]

FLAGS
  --mode choice            Set developer mode on or off. (choices: on, off)
  --user-id string         User id to act as or filter by. Without it, commands that act as a user use the test user id of this directory (for its own project), then the global one, and name it on stderr.
  --project-name string    Developer project to use instead of the one configured in this directory

INHERITED FLAGS
  --log-level choice    Define log level (choices: All, Fatal, Error, Warn, Info, Debug, Trace, None)

GLOBAL FLAGS
  --help, -h       Show help information
  --version, -v    Show version information

SUBCOMMANDS
  init                Initialize this directory with a developer project.
  playground-execute  Test tool executions against playground users using your developer project auth configs.
  listen              Listen to realtime trigger events for your developer project and optionally forward them into your local dev environment.
  logs                Inspect trigger and tool execution logs.
  toolkits            Discover and inspect Composio toolkits.
  auth-configs        View and manage Composio auth configs.
  connected-accounts  View and manage Composio connected accounts.
  triggers            Inspect and subscribe to trigger events.
  projects            Inspect developer projects and project context helpers.
EXAMPLES
  composio dev --mode on
  composio dev --mode off
DESCRIPTION
  Execute a tool by slug. Validates inputs against cached schemas and checks connections
automatically — just try it and it will tell you what to fix.

USAGE
  composio execute [flags] <slug> [<additional-slugs...>]

ARGUMENTS
  slug string              Tool slug (e.g. "GITHUB_CREATE_ISSUE")
  additional-slugs... string Additional tool slugs for --parallel (optional)

FLAGS
  --parallel, -p              Execute repeated tool slug/data groups concurrently
  --data, -d string           JSON arguments, @file, or - for stdin
  --file string               Inject a local file path into the single file_uploadable input
  --account string            Connected account selector for the inferred toolkit. Matches alias, word_id, or connected account id.
  --get-schema                Fetch and print the CLI-facing input schema without executing
  --dry-run                   Validate and preview the tool call without executing
  --skip-connection-check     Skip the connected-account check
  --skip-tool-params-check    Skip input validation against cached schema
  --skip-checks               Skip both connection and input validation checks

INHERITED FLAGS
  --log-level choice    Define log level (choices: All, Fatal, Error, Warn, Info, Debug, Trace, None)

GLOBAL FLAGS
  --help, -h       Show help information
  --version, -v    Show version information

EXAMPLES
  # Send an email
  composio execute GMAIL_SEND_EMAIL -d '{ recipient_email: "a@b.com", subject: "Hello", body: "World" }'

  # Create a GitHub issue with a named account
  composio execute GITHUB_CREATE_ISSUE --account work -d '{ owner: "acme", repo: "app", title: "Bug report", body: "Steps to reproduce..." }'

  # Preview what a tool call would send without executing
  composio execute SLACK_SEND_MESSAGE --dry-run -d '{ channel: "general", markdown_text: "Hello team" }'

  # Print the tool input schema as JSON (--help shows command options)
  composio execute GMAIL_SEND_EMAIL --get-schema

  # Read arguments from a file
  composio execute GITHUB_CREATE_ISSUE -d @issue.json

  # Execute multiple tools concurrently
  composio execute -p GMAIL_SEND_EMAIL -d '{ recipient_email: "a@b.com" }' GITHUB_CREATE_AN_ISSUE -d '{ owner: "acme", repo: "app", title: "Bug" }'

DESCRIPTION
  Connect an external account (GitHub, Gmail, Slack, etc.) so tools can act on your behalf.
Opens a browser for OAuth authorization and waits for confirmation.

USAGE
  composio dev connected-accounts link [flags] [<toolkit>]

ARGUMENTS
  toolkit string    Toolkit slug to link (e.g. "github", "gmail") (optional)

FLAGS
  --auth-config string    Auth config ID (e.g. "ac_..."). Uses legacy flow (no Tool Router).
  --no-wait               Do not wait for authorization; only print link info
  --no-browser            Do not open the browser automatically; print the URL to open manually
  --alias string          Alias to assign to the connected account. Required when creating an additional account for the same toolkit/auth config.
  --list                  List existing connected accounts for the toolkit instead of creating a new link

INHERITED FLAGS
  --log-level choice       Define log level (choices: All, Fatal, Error, Warn, Info, Debug, Trace, None)
  --user-id string         User id to act as or filter by. Without it, commands that act as a user use the test user id of this directory (for its own project), then the global one, and name it on stderr.
  --project-name string    Developer project to use instead of the one configured in this directory

GLOBAL FLAGS
  --help, -h       Show help information
  --version, -v    Show version information

EXAMPLES
  composio link github
  composio link gmail --alias work
  composio link github --list
